Cofiniteness of a numerical semigroup guarantees that each nonzero residue class modulo the multiplicity m contains some element of S, and well-ordering gives a unique least such element w_r. Using the definition Ap(S,m) = {s in S : s-m not in S}, one shows that 0 and the w_r all lie in the Apéry set, and conversely any element of the Apéry set must be either 0 or the least representative of its residue class. Finally, because w_r ≡ r mod m and m is the smallest positive element of S, each w_r has the unique form r + mk_r with k_r > 0.

The proof gives the standard Apéry-set argument: each nonzero residue class modulo the multiplicity has a nonempty fiber in S by cofiniteness, hence a unique least element w_r; it proves both inclusions for Ap(S,m) = {0,w_1,...,w_{m-1}}; and it derives the representation w_r = r + m k_r with uniqueness and positivity of k_r.
